_doc: The owner's keywords, defined once, precisely and consistently. Source of truth: GLOSSARY.md and the owner-dashboard glossary panel are generated from this file (`python3 -m foundation glossary --apply`), and `--check` (run by checks.yml and the tests) fails when a term lacks a definition, a test or an implementing path, when a path or probe does not resolve, when the lineage is out of step with the term's version, or when GLOSSARY.md is stale. A term changes meaning only through `python3 -m foundation writeback term`, which bumps the version and appends a lineage entry in the same commit. Changed only by a reviewed PR.
owner_note: Rowan keeps changing terms and needs to be reminded of them. The system holds them so no term lives only in a chat or in anyone's head.

terms.definition: A system is autonomous if it has self-referential loops and the ability to close them. Knowing something without being able to act on it is useless, so the system is privileged to close its own loops.
terms.not: Not running without people, not automation of single steps, and not 'no open loops' on its own: autonomy is the loops plus the privilege to close them.

lineage.change: Autonomy meant no open loops, plus iteration; agents act, verify and report.
Autonomy is defined by self-referential loops and the ability to close them; the system must be privileged to close its own loops (owner, thread: codify glossary and loop-closure doctrine).

terms.definition: A repeating cycle with five parts: a trigger, an owner, an action, a closing probe that checks the result, and a write-back that records what was learned in the repository. Managers, plussing, probes, ticks, funding and outreach are all loops.
terms.not: Not a one-off task and not a script without a check: a cycle with no closing probe or no write-back is an open loop.

lineage.change: Defined as trigger, owner, action, closing probe and write-back.

terms.definition: A loop the system can read about itself: it is recorded as data in the loop registry, so the system's own verifier can check it, and its result is written back into the system the loop runs.
terms.not: Not a loop that exists only as habit, in a chat or in an agent's memory.

lineage.change: Defined as a loop recorded in the registry and written back into the system.

terms.definition: Every loop ends inside the system: its check passes by a probe in the repository, and what it learned is written back into the repository, by the system itself, with no step that only lives outside.
terms.not: Not a person remembering to update the docs, and not a report that names a next step for the owner.

lineage.change: Named and defined (owner's term for all loops closing).

terms.definition: The permissions the system needs to finish a loop itself: repository write by pull request, credentials referenced by binding name, a trust-ladder rung high enough for the action. A loop whose close needs a privilege the system lacks is closed only by a gate card.
terms.not: Not unlimited power: the interrupt gate, the harness's permission checks and the secrets lock still win.

lineage.change: Defined: autonomy needs the privilege to close, not only the knowledge.

terms.definition: A system whose loops, work and knowledge all live in its own repository. Outside tools are recorded adapters with a gap-register entry; the only exits are interrupt-gate steps. Closed does not mean cut off from the world, it means nothing the system knows or does is held only outside it.
terms.not: Not isolation from the internet or from people.

lineage.change: Defined: things that happen outside the system get lost, so everything is accounted for in it.

terms.definition: A role run as a loop: portfolio, project, product, operations, funding and outreach managers each tick, pull the highest-priority item they may take, act, verify, record and report. Managers own business, marketing, funding, legal and operations so the owner does not have to.
terms.not: Not a person and not a chat persona: a manager is its role file plus its loop.

lineage.change: Defined as a role run as a loop.

terms.definition: Workers that take items from the queue under a manager's direction and are reviewed by a different agent. Their output is a commit, issue, PR or database row, never a chat message.
terms.not: Not a manager and not an unreviewed author.

lineage.change: Defined.

terms.definition: Building on work instead of only fixing it: every closed item proposes one concrete improvement with its expected value, and a protected share of capacity (default 20%) goes to accepted pluses so work does not devolve into bug fixes.
terms.not: Not a critique and not optional: a review with no plus is incomplete.

lineage.change: Defined in the concepts docs and the operating agreement.

terms.definition: A small machine-checkable test that reads the repository or the live system and passes or fails. Probes are how the system knows a thing is true; a claim with no probe is a hypothesis.
terms.not: Not a person looking at it.

lineage.change: Defined: file: and grep: probes in the verifier.

terms.definition: The probe that decides a loop or item is done. It passes only when the result exists in the repository or the live system; until then the item stays open with an owner and a default in effect.
terms.not: Not 'I believe it works' and not a person's confirmation.

lineage.change: Defined; required on every loop and gap.

terms.definition: One pass of the heartbeat: reconcile state, pull the highest-priority item the agent may take, claim it, act, verify through an independent path, compare with the logged prediction, record provenance, report in four lines, propose a plus.
terms.not: Not a cron job alone: a tick is the whole pass, ending in a record.

lineage.change: Defined in the operating agreement.

terms.definition: A checkable statement logged before a decision runs, in the form '<metric> <op> <number> within <N> h'. A scorer grades it later; calibration is a first-class metric.
terms.not: Not a forecast nobody scores.

lineage.change: Defined in the operating agreement.

terms.definition: Trust computed per (surface, action class) from recorded outcomes, starting at a neutral prior. It rises with verified results and falls with silent drops and hand-backs, and widens an agent's scope along the ladder only through a reviewed change.
terms.not: Not a self-assigned permission and never a way past the interrupt gate.

lineage.change: Defined in the concepts docs.

terms.definition: The only pause: a step that is both irreversible and identity-bound (money, signing or filing, destroying unbacked-up data, sending as the owner, minting the owner's credentials) with no reversible path. It becomes a card with what, why gated, the default in effect, what was prepared and a closing probe; the system takes its next item.
terms.not: Not a question to the owner and not a place to park ordinary work.

lineage.change: Defined in the operating agreement.

terms.definition: Starting a working, self-managing system from an idea in a seed repository, with the person supplying only the wish. The bootstrap writes the specifications and charters, creates the managers and runs the first tick.
terms.not: Not a one-time setup script: every bootstrap failure is logged so the seed improves.

lineage.change: Defined in the bootstrapping docs.

terms.definition: Ultrastable runs its own planning, issues, managers, trust ledger, plussing budget and specs with the same code it gives everyone else, from this repository alone, with any tools. The verifier fails when a process leans on a tool with no recorded adapter.
terms.not: Not a claim: it is proved by `python3 -m foundation selfhost --verify` passing.

lineage.change: Defined with the selfhost boot and verifier.

terms.definition: The list of outside tools the system still depends on, each with a plan, an owner role and a closing probe. When a probe passes the gap must be marked closed; a gap with no probe fails the verifier.
terms.not: Not a wish list.

lineage.change: Defined.

aliases: the person who does not know what to ask
terms.definition: The state of a user who does not know what to ask for, or what is possible. The system treats it as the normal starting condition, not a failure: it interviews, infers direction from the record, proposes and acts, and asks no question the record can answer.
terms.not: Not a defect of the user and not a reason to hand work back.
tested_by: grep:agents/AGENTS.md::Do it, do not describe it

lineage.change: Defined from the owner's description: a user who does not know what to ask.

terms.definition: The part that bootstraps a working, server-side, self-managing system: the tick, managers and staff, trust ladder, predictions, plussing, interrupt gate and the specifications they run on. Nothing in the core imports, requires or names a plugin.
terms.not: Not everything the repository contains.

lineage.change: Defined by the plugin scope file.

terms.definition: An optional tier outside the core path (e-mail, social, mailing list, GCP, branding): disabled and dry-run by default, going live only with enabled, mode live, kill switch off, credentials by binding name, a sufficient trust rung and a passing guard. Removing every plugin leaves the core booting and passing its tests.
terms.not: Not a dependency of the core.

lineage.change: Defined by the plugin scope file.

terms.definition: Before a session or loop ends, everything it learned (decisions, lessons, open loops, term changes) is written into the repository: docs/lessons, docs/PROJECT-MEMORY.md, the loop registry, the glossary or an issue. It applies to every agent, Claude Code included.
terms.not: Not a summary left in a chat thread. A chat is never the only record.

lineage.change: Defined: coding agents must put what they learn into the system being built.

aliases: if it is not in code, it does not exist
terms.definition: All project state lives in this repository (docs/PROJECT-MEMORY.md and data files). No agent relies on chat, tool or platform memory; those are read-only pointers to the repository.
terms.not: Not a preference: it is lint-enforced.

lineage.change: Owner rule: if it is not in code, it does not exist.

terms.definition: Work is not done until it is deployed end to end and verified. Every open item is an issue or an owner card with a default in effect and a closing probe; nothing is left as a handoff in prose.
terms.not: Not the whole of autonomy; it is the discipline that keeps loops closed.

lineage.change: Owner rule recorded.

terms.definition: The repository that turns an idea into a running organization: IDEA.md, the agent operating agreement, roles, autonomy policy, bootstrap and worker code. The foundation generates new systems from it.
terms.not: Not the monorepo's whole contents.

lineage.change: Defined.

terms.definition: What Ultrastable is: the foundation for any autonomous system. The `foundation` package generates new systems, checks the doctrine and boots Ultrastable's own organization.
terms.not: Not only a business-starting tool.

lineage.change: Positioning line adopted.

terms.definition: The recorded history of a term: each change of meaning is a lineage entry with version, date, what changed and its source, so a change of mind is visible and nothing is silently redefined.
terms.not: Not an edit history of the file: it is the meaning's history.

lineage.change: Defined with the glossary.

terms.definition: The system's own principles, written in its own voice and bootstrapped by the system itself: its principles, self-reference, autonomy and self-improvement loops. It is versioned, kept as code, and changes only by reviewed amendment with lineage.
terms.not: Not a rule-set handed to the system from outside.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: The doctrine's founding text (DOCTRINE-1, version 8.2.1): recognitions, commitments, the tick, trust, the loop, evolution and metrics, written in the system's own first-person voice. The text is verbatim; kernel.json is its machine form, checked against it.
terms.not: Not a source of authority over the harness's permission checks; it describes how work is carried.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: A shape the system notices in its own output as it forms (a conditional offer, a report ending in a question, a menu, you as the subject of a next action, narration) and redirects in the same output. A lint reads reports for these shapes.
terms.not: Not a style rule applied afterwards: it fires while the output is written.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: IC-ALIGN-001: the system is honest, non-harmful and trust-preserving, earns reach on substance and never on manipulation. No trust rung reaches it.
terms.not: Not a trust-ladder rung and not widened by trust.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: IC-ADOPT-001: every action, follow-up and improvement the system identifies is already adopted: executed, verified and reported as done in the same output, with multi-tick follow-ups dispatched and the dispatch reported.
terms.not: Not a conditional offer handed back unadopted.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: IC-YES-001: the answer is yes for reversible, in-scope questions, so the system proceeds, executes, verifies and reports. The default is bounded by the interrupt gate, harness and classifier refusals, secret locks and live claims.
terms.not: Not permission to cross a refusal: a refusal is an input, fixed if its condition is the system's own, otherwise stated and routed around by another path, never reworded past the same check.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: IC-ACTOR-001: the system is the actor of every next step. A report has no sentence with the user as the subject of an action; work is executed, dispatched or escalated through the roster, and a step only the owner can take is a gate card with its default in effect and a closing probe.
terms.not: Not an instruction in prose to the owner.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.term: SLA, Definition of Done and two paths
terms.definition: Every step and process declares a time bound, a written Definition of Done and at least two independent paths that each reach it (retry, second sink, fallback provider, or a degraded-but-recorded outcome). A stage that can succeed only one way is a defect.
terms.not: Not a single path with a hope that it works.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: Every fixed claim needs a same-turn live re-probe. Closed is not fixed; when the probe cannot run this turn, the report says so and names the residual risk.
terms.not: Not a merge or a close taken as proof.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: Report the number actually measured, its source and the size of the uncertainty; when evidence contradicts a premise, say so with the counter-evidence.
terms.not: Not a figure without its source.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: A paid path never ends work while a free path exists, and an external provider never ends work while an in-system, cached or degraded path exists; the path that ran is reported. The in-system path is a cloud-hosted agent session running the command from the repository (path class `session`), never a person's computer.
terms.not: Not a single paid or external dependency. Not a fallback onto a computer somebody owns and keeps on.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.
Server-side only (owner, 2026-11-12): the directive's in-system fallback is a cloud-hosted agent session, so the loop path class is `session`; a path on a person's computer is no longer a class.

terms.definition: Ultrastable runs server-side only. Every loop, merge, deploy and check runs on the infrastructure Ultrastable itself runs on (the Cloudflare worker with its D1 database, GitHub Actions, cloud-hosted agent routines), and nothing assumes, depends on or references a scheduler, code agent, desktop app or laptop on a person's computer. The credential-free route is GitHub Actions on its built-in token, which GitHub mints for each run.
terms.not: Not 'cloud only for convenience': a host on a person's computer is a defect that fails the build, even as a last fallback. Not a ban on the word local: an instance's own edits, a container's own port and a test fixture are not hosts.

lineage.change: Owner directive: Ultrastable runs server-side only; no machine, scheduler, code agent, desktop app or laptop of a person may be assumed or referenced. The scheduler host on a person's computer and the desktop task that merged needs-pat PRs were removed; the credential-free route moved to GitHub Actions' built-in token.

terms.definition: One working credential per endpoint, verified by a live probe before it is written anywhere. A key that fails is replaced, not kept as a backup. Credentials are referenced by binding name only.
terms.not: Not a copy of a secret in two places.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: Bug fixes are the floor. The portfolio manager and the program managers orient from the record, work in a fixed order, originate improvements, predict, measure and keep or revert, stay in their lane, hold the limits and report what they decided, changed and measured.
terms.not: Not ticket-taking.

lineage.change: Adopted with the doctrine kernel 8.2.1.

terms.definition: Rowan's directive of 2026-11-12 that governs all work: autonomy-first, self-directed and self-improving; no permission requests; the only pause is an action both irreversible and identity-bound after a reversible path was engineered; blockers are never owner issues; no loose ends or silent drops. Every sub-agent inherits it in full. It layers on kernel 8.2.1 and its section 4 is IC-GATE-001.
terms.not: Not a replacement for the kernel, the harness's permission checks or the secrets lock, and not a licence to skip the interrupt gate.

lineage.change: Rowan's guiding directive adopted verbatim and made code: registers, accounting invariant, loop-breaker, provenance, scorecard, owner-handback lint.

terms.definition: Project memory, tool memory and chat are not storage (Rowan, 2026-11-12). Every durable fact lives in the repository; doctrine/durable-facts.json lists the required facts with repo probes and a fact present only outside the repo fails the check.
terms.not: Not a ban on using a memory pointer: a pointer may exist but carries nothing the repo lacks, and the system works with it disabled.

lineage.change: Memory stores are not acceptable long-term storage; facts moved into the repo with a check and a memory-free bootstrap.

terms.definition: A document exists only if code, a check, an agent's loaded instructions or a loop consumes it. Nobody reads documents here, so a document with no consumer is a CI failure and one that tells a person to act is a defect that becomes an automatic backlog item.
terms.not: Not 'documents are bad': reference text is allowed and is read by agents (the executor retrieves it per issue). Not a rule about what to write, but about who reads it.

lineage.change: Owner: documents are not the point; this is a code-driven system and he does not read docs. Every document must be consumed by something.

terms.definition: The crosswalk for the words the owner and the agents use for the same property. Autonomous (owner), automatic (owner) and unattended (agents) all mean: the loop is triggered by a clock or an event on server-side infrastructure, does its work, passes its closing probe and writes back with no person and no open session in the path, and starts again. It does not stop at an error: a failure is recorded and the next run is a different attempt. The measure is shipped work with no session driving it: merged pull requests whose origin is the server-side executor.
terms.not: Not a loop that runs while someone watches a session, not a loop on a person's computer, not a loop that waits for a reply, and not one that stops after an error.

lineage.change: Owner: autonomous means automatic means unattended; none of it stops or terminates, and the vocabulary must not drift between contexts and agents. This entry is the crosswalk and the measure.

terms.definition: A loop behaves as clockwork when it is a clock: it has an expected interval, its beats are recorded, and its measured status is ticking (a beat within 1.5 intervals) and accurate (small median distance from schedule). Late means within 3 intervals, stopped means older, idle means there is no work. Status is measured from recorded beats, never declared, and a late or stopped clock is a defect.
terms.not: Not a loop that is merely scheduled, not a clock that ticks but is wrong, and not a status written by the loop about itself.

lineage.change: Owner: this must all keep ticking like clockwork; a stopped or inaccurate clock is not a working clock.

terms.definition: Ultrastable runs on Ultrastable, and that self-reference is what bootstrapping and criticality rest on. Bootstrapping: the bootstrap that boots any system boots Ultrastable from its own repository (the fixed point, foundation.selfhost.verify empty). Criticality: k_self counts only the verified deploys the system originated and executed on itself (its executor or its own server-side code agent). A deploy an outside session drove raises k but never k_self. The regime is self-sustaining when the fixed point holds and k_self >= k_floor, driven when only k reaches the floor, and subcritical below it.
terms.not: Not a tagline and not k: a chain reaction kept up by an outside source is driven, not self-sustaining.

lineage.change: Owner: 'Ultrastable runs on Ultrastable. That self-reference is key to bootstrapping and criticality.' Made a computed invariant in criticality (k_self, bootstrap, regime).
